documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy: how it applies to generative AI
documents.stance_why: The page says "what is permitted depends on your course" and quotes the policy that permitted AI use "may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment"; it sets no default itself and leaves the decision to courses and assignments, so delegates.
documents.summary: Explains that Syracuse's Academic Integrity Policy leaves AI permissions to each course and assignment, and that students remain responsible for the work. Defines generative AI and says users must review and make AI content their own.

units.why: This page applies the Academic Integrity Policy to generative AI. The quoted sentence says permitted AI use "may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment", so the rule is left to each course and assignment; it is a statement of fact about variation, hence P04 (not P85, which concerns schools or units).
units.anchor: may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment

units.why: This page applies the Academic Integrity Policy to generative AI. The same sentence says the variation rests "on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment", tying AI decisions to learning objectives, which is P83 (not P04, which says who decides).
units.anchor: based on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment
units.policy: AI permission is based on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment.

units.why: The page defines the tools it governs: "These tools generate new content based on existing data from the internet or other databases". This sets what generative AI means for the guidance, so it is a definition (P61), informs.
units.anchor: These tools generate new content

units.why: "Generative AI requires human input, editing and evaluation" says AI work needs a human to direct and judge it, keeping the person as the thinker (P32); a general principle so informs. P31 is not chosen because it concerns verifying correctness, which the next sentence covers.
units.anchor: Generative AI requires human input, editing and evaluation.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this sentence; coder B did not. The source says "Generative AI requires human input, editing and evaluation." It states that AI work needs a human to direct and judge it, a separate principle from the verification duty in the next sentence. Kept as P32, informs.

units.why: "It is our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy" is a duty to verify AI output (P31). Modality is must because "responsibility" is stated as an obligation. The "make it our own" clause is coded separately as P29.
units.anchor: review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy
units.policy: Users are responsible for reviewing and revising AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy.
units.resolution_why: Coder A anchored on the whole clause and split off "make it our own"; coder B coded one P31 unit on the sentence. Both gave P31, all, during-work, must. Anchor shortened here to the verification clause so the two units do not share an anchor.

units.why: The same sentence adds that users must "make it our own", i.e. the content they use is theirs. That is ownership of work (P29), separate from the verification duty above.
units.anchor: make it our own
units.policy: Users are responsible for making AI-generated content their own.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A split "make it our own" from the verification duty. The source joins them in one sentence ("to ensure its accuracy and make it our own"), but ownership of the content is a distinct rule (P29) from checking accuracy (P31). Kept as a separate unit.

units.why: The page subtitle says "the responsibility for the work stays with you", placing responsibility for the work on students (P29). Modality is must, consistent with how the same page treats "our responsibility" as an obligation.
units.anchor: the responsibility for the work stays with you
units.resolution_why: Coder A said informs, coder B said must; actor student, phase general and type P29 agree. The sentence states who bears responsibility for the work. Because responsibility is an obligation on the student (and P31 on the same page is coded must), final modality is must.

notes: syracuse-u2 saved text is the Academic Integrity Resources index; it contains no generative-AI rule ("AI" there means Academic Integrity), so only the MySlice acknowledgment unit (UNCOVERED, general integrity) was kept. The three-statement syllabus requirement described in the collect file is not in the saved text and was not coded. Coder B also coded four general academic-integrity units on this page, dropped because they are not about AI: "Academic Integrity Syllabus Requirements" (P09, a link title, fit note: required syllabus language is listed as a resource but AI is not mentioned); "Most cases are reported by faculty and instructors via an online reporting system" (P81, fit note: general integrity cases, AI not named); "Students and other University community members are encouraged to report possible violations" (P71, fit note: reporting integrity violations generally, not AI-specific); "informs them of their appeal rights" (P64, fit note: appeal rights for any integrity charge, not AI-specific). Coder A fit notes kept: study planning and group-study organization are not practice problems or summaries (P14); office-hours preparation uses AI to prepare for human help (P72). The ITS page (u3) overlaps u1 on the quoted rule and the review duty.
